msg: (A) the susceptance null IS the best setting: RL at the null minus RL at 0.90x the null total C = +3.275 dB. This underwrites the 'trimmer at its best setting' premise of s11_band.cir and s11_corners.cir, which is otherwise an assertion.
(A) same test 10% ABOVE the null: +3.275 dB. Symmetric with dopt_m10 to 5 decimal places, which is what a true minimum of |Gamma| looks like.
(A) 0.80x the null total C costs 7.406 dB.
(A) 1.25x the null total C costs 9.050 dB.

(A) the scaling test is run at L = 30 nH precisely so the trimmer sits mid-range - 7.194 pF of a delivered 1-30 pF part, with room to move +/-25% in both directions without hitting a stop. A test run at the as-routed 7.21 nH would need negative trimmer values and would prove nothing.
(B) THE V2 ASSERTION, low end: total shunt C with the DELIVERED Johanson 5602 (parts/5602.json: 1-30 pF) at full CCW = 4.7 pF port + 1 pF trimmer = 5.70 pF.

(B) THE V2 ASSERTION, high end: full CW = 4.7 + 30 = 34.70 pF. The retired bench used cmax = 35 pF, which matches NO part on the BOM (it was inherited from the retired BFC280811339, a 3-33 pF part); that would read 39.70 pF here.

(B) README NUMBER - the smallest residual series L the delivered trimmer can null EXACTLY, at the nominal 4.7 pF port: 14.279 nH. The as-routed board is 7.21 nH, i.e. BELOW this, which is the whole of review-verify V1.

(B) README NUMBER - the largest residual L the delivered trimmer can null exactly: 94.376 nH. The stale bench said 99.64 nH (1.3 pF port + a 35 pF trimmer) and a 35 pF trimmer against the corrected 4.7 pF port would say 111.41 nH; both are outside this window, so this bound catches either half of V2 being reverted.
(B) the same low endpoint as series reactance at 25.0 MHz: 2.243 ohm.

(B) the same high endpoint as series reactance: 14.825 ohm. Note it is BELOW the 16.24 ohm point where Reff alone would break 26 dB at R = 50 (reff_limit.cir xcap_r50_ohm), so at nominal resistance the trimmer's top stop, not the resistance transformation, is what ends the exact-null range.
(B) README NUMBER - achievable adjustment range, exact-null definition: 80.10 nH wide (14.28 to 94.38 nH).

(B) the window at the OPTIMISTIC end of the port-parasitic band (3.5 pF): low edge 11.264 nH. There is no field solver on this pipeline, so the 4.7 pF estimate is swept; the window moves with it and the README range should be quoted as 14.3-94.4 nH nominal with an 11.3-98.6 nH envelope.
(B) high edge at 3.5 pF: 90.523 nH.

(B) low edge at the PESSIMISTIC 6.0 pF: 17.553 nH. This is the number that sets how much series inductance a two-sided-null respin would have to add to be safe against the parasitic uncertainty (see block E).
(B) high edge at 6.0 pF: 98.643 nH. The window WIDTH is nearly parasitic-independent (79.3 / 80.1 / 81.1 nH across the band); it is the position that moves.

(B) simulated proof, not just algebra: at L = lnull_lo with the trimmer pinned at its 1 pF stop the null is REAL, not a clamped mistune - 59.96 dB, whose entire residual is Reff = 50 + X^2/R = 50.10 ohm.

(B) same at the top: L = lnull_hi with the trimmer at its 30 pF stop gives 27.51 dB. The top of the exact-null range still clears crit. 2 by 1.5 dB, so the whole 14.28-94.38 nH window is spec-legal at nominal resistance.
(B) same check at the 6.0 pF parasitic: 56.37 dB.

(B) and the tightest corner of the window analysis: top of the window at the pessimistic parasitic, 26.78 dB - still above crit. 2, but by only 0.78 dB. A build whose residual is near 98 nH is spec-legal and has no margin.
(B) 64.07 dB at the 3.5 pF low edge.
(B) 28.21 dB at the 3.5 pF high edge.

(C) HOW FAR BELOW THE WINDOW THE BOARD SITS: lnull_lo - L_as_routed = 14.279 - 7.21 = 7.069 nH. C1 bottoms out and has upward-only authority. A negative or near-zero reading means the board has entered the window and the README's 'no null to find' language must be retracted.
(C) crit. 2 at the low stop, R = 50: 39.12 dB. Cross-checks s11_band.cir rl_r50_p47_fc and s11_corners.cir rl_r50_l721 - three independent instantiations, same number.

(C) WRONG-VALUE TRIPWIRE, mirroring s11_band.cir rl_r50_p47_fc: the low-stop nominal build must read 39.12 dB. With the stale 1.3 pF port this block would read 52.76 dB. Cross-bench consistency on this one number is what ties the three benches to the same model.
(C) crit. 2 at the low stop, R = 52.5 (+5% catalogue corner): 31.19 dB.
(C) crit. 2 at the low stop, R = 52.5 AND the pessimistic 6.0 pF port: 30.37 dB - the worst credible as-built number anywhere in these four benches.

(C) the hypothetical perfect null at the +5% corner - a physically unbuildable 2.883 pF total, less than the port parasitic alone - reads 32.173 dB. This is the ceiling the low stop is being measured against.
(C) the same hypothetical at R = 50: 71.82 dB. This is the number README s4's R_eff table quotes; it is NOT achievable on this board, and cost_r50 below is the difference.

(C) THE ANSWER TO 'WHAT DOES BOTTOMING OUT COST': 0.983 dB at the +5% resistance corner, the corner that actually binds the spec. That is the entire price of having no null to tune - under one decibel out of 5.19 dB of margin.
(C) the same cost at the optimistic 3.5 pF port: 0.394 dB.
(C) and at the pessimistic 6.0 pF port: 1.799 dB. Across the whole parasitic uncertainty band the cost of the bottomed-out trimmer at the binding corner stays under 2 dB.

(C) at NOMINAL resistance the same cost reads 32.70 dB, which sounds catastrophic and is not: it is the gap between 0.0000066% and 0.0123% of reflected power. Both are three orders of magnitude inside a 26 dB (0.25%) spec. The dB difference is large only because a perfect null on a perfect 50 ohm load is a singularity. Reported as a window rather than a max so that a bench which has quietly stopped clamping the trimmer (which would drive this to ~0) also fails.
(D) L = 1 pH, i.e. NO launch inductance at all, trimmer at its stop: 33.00 dB. Spec is met with the residual completely absent - the 4.7 pF port alone never breaks 26 dB.
(D) L = 14.28 nH, the window's low edge: 59.95 dB.
(D) L = 94.38 nH, the window's high edge: 27.51 dB (identical to rl_null_hi, as it must be).
(D) L = 100 nH: 26.46 dB. Past the exact-null window - the trimmer is hard against its 30 pF stop - but still above spec, which is why SPEC authority is wider than NULL authority.
(D) L = 102 nH: 26.065 dB. Tight bracket, warning severity by design: this pins the upper edge of spec authority to 0.065 dB, finer than any bound should fail a gate on.

(D) L = 103 nH: 25.869 dB - below spec. With rl_l102 this brackets the README NUMBER: at R = 50 with the delivered 1-30 pF trimmer, RL >= 26 dB holds out to L = 102-103 nH (closed-form crossing 102.33 nH, X = 16.07 ohm). The stale bench claimed ~103.2 nH from a 35 pF part.
(D) L = 110 nH: 24.51 dB. Past spec authority, and no trimmer setting recovers it.
(D) the same authority question at R = 52.5, where the resistance transformation bites long before the trimmer runs out of range: L = 70 nH gives 26.78 dB.

(D) L = 76.86 nH at R = 52.5: 26.000 dB. The +5% corner's spec authority ends at 76.9 nH - a third of the nominal-resistance figure - and it is set by Reff = R + X^2/R, not by the trimmer (reff_limit.cir lcap_r525_nh derives the same 76.86 nH from closed form with an IDEAL unlimited trimmer, and gets the same answer, which is the proof that the part is not the limit there).
(D) L = 80 nH at R = 52.5: 25.65 dB - fails, and no setting of C1 recovers it.

(E) THE ANSWER TO 'WHAT WOULD A TWO-SIDED NULL COST': the minimum series inductance that must be ADDED to reach the window is +7.069 nH (7.21 -> 14.28 nH), and that only lands the board exactly ON the low edge with zero downward authority. To be genuinely two-sided across the 3.5-6.0 pF parasitic band and the 49-52.5 ohm resistance range the target is >= 19.36 nH, i.e. about +12.1 nH.

(E) THE PRICE, and it is negative: adding 7.07 nH to reach the window's low edge IMPROVES return loss at the +5% corner by 0.716 dB (31.190 -> 31.906 dB). A true null beats an over-corrected low stop by more than the extra X^2/R costs. The intuition that 'more inductance is always worse' is wrong on this board because the fixed 4.7 pF port is already over-compensating.
(E) +10.34 nH (to 17.55 nH, the low edge at the pessimistic parasitic): +0.589 dB, still an improvement.
(E) +15.00 nH (to 22.21 nH, comfortably inside the window at every parasitic estimate): +0.315 dB, still an improvement.

(E) +22.79 nH (to 30 nH) is where the price finally turns negative: -0.257 dB at the +5% corner. So the whole useful two-sided-null respin range costs between -0.26 dB and +0.72 dB - i.e. nothing measurable. The real objection to the respin is mechanical (a meander at the 0.9392 mm current-limited minimum width, or a smaller solder lap on a 1.732 Arms joint), not electrical.
(E) +32.79 nH (to 40 nH): -1.155 dB. Beyond about +23 nH the added reactance costs more through Reff than the recovered null buys back.
(E) crit. 2 still holds at the +5% corner for the minimum respin: 31.91 dB.
(E) crit. 2 at the +5% corner for a 30 nH respin: 30.93 dB.
(E) 40 nH at the +5% corner: 30.04 dB. Even a wildly over-inductive respin has 4 dB of margin; the respin is not spec-limited anywhere in the useful range.
